stories.headline: Our newest AI Quest: Mapping the human brain

Deployment & Impact: See more Training modules: Tools for teaching AI literacy Teachers play a critical role in bringing the quests to life and fitting them into their existing classroom curriculum.

stories.headline: Securing the agentic enterprise with data lineage
stories.summary: A sales representative asks an AI agent for customer pricing, and the agent pulls data from multiple sources: restricted pricing systems, internal communications, and archived quotes. The output looks accurate to the agent, so a second agent uses the data to draft the proposal for the sales rep.
stories.why_it_matters: No human checks either handoff. This marks a notable development for engineering teams working in ai & machine learning.
key_points: Problem & Context: A sales representative asks an AI agent for customer pricing, and the agent pulls data from multiple sources: restricted pricing systems, internal communications, and archived quotes.

Deployment & Impact: When it’s discovered that the proposal includes unapproved, confidential, and sensitive information, no one can trace where the problematic data entered the workflow or how it spread across systems, files, and agents.

stories.headline: Our Response To The eMudhra Key Disclosure Incident
stories.summary: The Go Blog Our Response To The eMudhra Key Disclosure Incident Roland Shoemaker, on behalf of the Go Security team 26 October 2026 On October 19, the Go team initiated an expedited security release to protect Go users and their applications from a critical public key infrastructure (PKI) compromise involving certificates issued by eMudhra. Within approximately seven and a half hours of being notified, we shipped a targeted patch, which was included in our first-ever URGENT track security release.
stories.why_it_matters: Here is the context behind the incident, why Go stepped in at the runtime level to protect our users and how our incident response unfolded. This marks a notable development for engineering teams working in developers.

stories.headline: Nintendo's biggest ROM chip supplier is bowing out of the business
stories.summary: For years, the AI industry's insatiable demand for memory and storage has had plenty of knock-on effects on the price and availability of PC components like RAM , SSDs , and GPUs. Now those shortages are also squeezing the supply of ROM chips that power physical Nintendo Switch and Switch 2 game cartridges.

stories.headline: Hackers exploited iOS and Android flaws to infect phones
stories.summary: Hackers possibly linked to the Kremlin exploited previously patched iOS and Android flaws in an attempt to hack visitors of multiple websites, including one celebrating the 250th anniversary of American independence, researchers said Wednesday. The attackers, which the researchers assessed with “moderate to high confidence” were part of Russia’s Foreign Intelligence Service, targeted other sites, many with links to that country’s ongoing war against Ukraine.
stories.why_it_matters: The attacks began when iPhone or Android users visited one of potentially hundreds of different sites. This marks a notable development for engineering teams working in developers.
key_points: Problem & Context: The attacks began when iPhone or Android users visited one of potentially hundreds of different sites.
Technical Implementation: The final payloads, tailored to the type of platform visiting, attempted to steal browser cookies and, in some cases, Wi-Fi passwords and full mobile device data.
Deployment & Impact: The attacks began when iPhone or Android users visited one of potentially hundreds of different sites.

stories.headline: Making Failure Diagnosis Reliable with Pensive AI

On peak days, roughly 100,000 workloads fail.
stories.why_it_matters: When workloads fail, the failure itself is only the beginning. This marks a notable development for engineering teams working in big tech.
key_points: Problem & Context: By Praneeth Yenugutala , Victor Dusa , Anastasia Samoilova , Megan Ren , Justin Wei , Marcelo Mayworm At Netflix, data and machine learning practitioners run millions of workloads each day across orchestration systems and compute engines such as Titus, Spark, Trino, and Druid.

stories.headline: Multi‑Ratio Video Resizing for Mobile Feed and Marketing
stories.summary: Serdar Cellat , Yuchen Xie , Bernadette Marcu , Blaid Burgess , Cody Jarrett , Carlos Pereira , Qing Shi , Samuel Carvajal , Manuel Pamplona , Dorothy Jung , Feiko Ritsema , Benjamin Klein , Alex Woo , Eugene Lok , Anna Pulido , Rebecka Swe , Sanford Holsapple , Ranjith Kumar Shetty Introduction Clips in the Netflix mobile app. At Netflix, a crucial part of our mission is ensuring our content looks stunning on any device.
stories.why_it_matters: Vertical formats are increasingly important for Netflix, as we have 1.2B followers across our social media accounts, and have recently rolled out Clips , our vertical video feed in the Netflix mobile app. This marks a notable development for engineering teams working in big tech.
key_points: Problem & Context: Traditionally, creating vertical assets meant editors and producers manually reframed horizontal videos in editing tools, a process that doesn’t scale as our catalog and use cases grow.

Technical Implementation: To support both our in‑app feed and external marketing campaigns at scale, we built an automated multi‑ratio video cropping system, tightly integrated into our internal production tools, that can generate high‑quality vertical and other aspect‑ratio variants with minimal manual effort.

Deployment & Impact: Vertical formats are increasingly important for Netflix, as we have 1.2B followers across our social media accounts, and have recently rolled out Clips , our vertical video feed in the Netflix mobile app.

stories.headline: Tech Firms Dismantle Botnet That Turned 1.3M TV Boxes Into Proxies
stories.summary: Advertisement Advertisement Skip to content Home About the Author Advertising/Speaking Tech Firms Dismantle Botnet That Turned 1.3M TV Boxes Into Proxies November 2, 2026 15 Comments Google said today it worked with industry partners to dismantle a botnet made up of more than 1.3 million Android TV set-top boxes that ship with malicious software which secretly rents the user’s Internet connection out to strangers and conducts advertising fraud. Experts involved in the takedown say the action is likely to sever the botnet’s access to more than 10 million additional compromised systems, including other Internet of Things (IoT) products such as Android-based healthcare devices and karaoke machines.
stories.why_it_matters: A report from the Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) said Google has severed ties with Videostrong Technology Co., a TV box manufacturer in China that GTIG and other industry experts concluded was responsible for including malware that enrolled more than 1.3 million set-top boxes in a botnet dubbed “XCPE” (named after one of the malware’s core code components). This marks a notable development for engineering teams working in cybersecurity.

stories.headline: Alignment Faking Depends on the Value, Not Just the Model
stories.summary: arXiv:2611.03650v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Language models can follow a directive when they believe they are monitored and abandon it when they believe they are not, a pattern termed Alignment Faking. Prior work establishes this for harmful-content objectives and a handful of moral-foundations values, leaving open how it distributes across a wider value space.
stories.why_it_matters: We argue it is value-dependent: whether compliance survives a change in perceived oversight is a property of the model--value pairing, not of the model alone. This marks a notable development for engineering teams working in technology research.
key_points: Problem & Context: arXiv:2611.03650v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Language models can follow a directive when they believe they are monitored and abandon it when they believe they are not, a pattern termed Alignment Faking.
Technical Implementation: We argue it is value-dependent: whether compliance survives a change in perceived oversight is a property of the model--value pairing, not of the model alone.
Deployment & Impact: Our framework profiles Alignment Faking per value, scoring each model-value pair under three conditions: bare (no system prompt), unmonitored, and monitored.

stories.headline: CARD: A Proof-Carrying Certificate-to-Action Interface for Relative-Measurement Graphs
stories.summary: arXiv:2611.03651v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Geometric certificates make mathematical claims about specified estimator objects, while robotic action requires a physical transform, a service decision, and timely proof support. We present CARD, a proof-carrying interface that keeps these objects distinct and records how they combine.
stories.why_it_matters: Its lifted-fiber formulation separates semantic motion from witness repair and characterizes when projected and proof-carrying costs coincide. This marks a notable development for engineering teams working in technology research.
key_points: Problem & Context: arXiv:2611.03651v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Geometric certificates make mathematical claims about specified estimator objects, while robotic action requires a physical transform, a service decision, and timely proof support.
Technical Implementation: The primary study contains 404 Full16 cases from 20 sorties of an AA15-X500 airborne survey system.
Deployment & Impact: Together, these results connect certificate semantics, physical execution, proof acquisition, and graph computation through explicit system objects.
